race.name: Bootlegger 100
race.tagline: Wilson Creek Gorge, Maple Sally Road, and 7,250 feet of climbing across the official 85-mile North Carolina long course.

vitals.start_format: Neutral police-led rollout from downtown Lenoir before open-road racing
vitals.registration: Open on BikeReg; $105 for either distance when reviewed
vitals.prize_purse: Overall and division awards; equal King of Pisgah series payouts for men and women
vitals.aid_stations: Organizer-stocked rest areas with water and food; no drop-bag service
route_options: 85 miles with approximately 7,250 feet of climbing
58 miles with approximately 4,500 feet of climbing

climate.description: Mid-April mountain weather can shift during an all-day ride; use the final Lenoir and Wilson Creek Gorge forecast.
challenges: Rain can make gravel descents slick

terrain.primary: Western North Carolina mountain gravel with sustained climbing and technical descents
terrain.surface: The current 85-mile course leaves downtown Lenoir on country roads, enters the Grandfather Ranger District, and uses Wilson Creek Gorge and Maple Sally Road. The organizer does not publish a current surface percentage.

biased_opinion.summary: The Bootlegger is a timed, open-road gravel race from downtown Lenoir into Wilson Creek Gorge and the Grandfather Ranger District. The official 2027 long course is 85 miles with approximately 7,250 feet of climbing; the 58-mile course still carries about 4,500 feet. Maple Sally Road, long descents, self-supported race rules, and a 13-hour finish window make this a serious mountain day without pretending the retired 100-mile alignment is still current.
strengths: Wilson Creek Gorge and Grandfather Ranger District scenery
weaknesses: Approximately 7,250 feet of climbing in 85 miles
No outside support or drop bags
Spring rain can change descent grip
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Choose the 85-mile Bootlegger if you want a hard, technically meaningful mountain-gravel race with real organizer history and modest production gloss. Choose the 58 only if 4,500 feet still sounds like the shorter option you actually want.

logistics.alternate_airports: Regional air options vary; a car is required for practical event access
logistics.lodging_note: The organizer lists a Lenoir hotel and permits self-contained overnight vehicle camping in designated downtown lots.
logistics.parking: Hundreds of downtown Lenoir spaces are available in the organizer-marked lots.
logistics.packet_pickup: Friday 5:00-10:00 PM or Saturday 5:30-7:30 AM at 1016 Harper Avenue.
logistics.travel_summary: Sign-in, start, and finish use separate downtown Lenoir addresses a few blocks apart. Arrive early enough to park, sign in, and attend the 7:45 AM racer meeting.
logistics.food_options: Stocked rest areas are provided, followed by a post-race meal and refreshments.
logistics.camping: Self-contained RV, van, and car camping is authorized in designated downtown lots; no hookups are provided.

course_description.character: The official 85-mile route combines approximately 7,250 feet of climbing with country roads, Wilson Creek Gorge, Grandfather Ranger District gravel, Maple Sally Road, and long mountain descents.

suffering_zones.name: Grandfather Ranger District and Maple Sally Road
suffering_zones.description: The 85-mile route keeps climbing after the distance split and reaches Maple Sally Road before returning to Lenoir.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Use low enough gearing to stay seated, keep early climbing below the red line, and preserve fueling discipline for Maple Sally.

suffering_zones.name: Mountain gravel descents
suffering_zones.description: Historical rider reports describe loose, slick gravel and sustained braking; the official course remains open to traffic.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Brake before corners, leave sight-line margin, and choose tires and pressure for control rather than a clean-road speed test.

course_description.signature_challenge: Approximately 7,250 feet of climbing across 85 miles, with Maple Sally Road and technical descents late enough to punish poor pacing.

history.reputation: A long-running Western North Carolina mountain-gravel race known for Wilson Creek Gorge, Maple Sally Road, sustained climbing, and difficult descents.

eligibility.status_note: Pisgah Productions confirms a timed 2027 gravel race with registration open, two scored distances, current course demands, rules, schedule, and results history. This is distinct from the unrelated Georgia trail-running event using the old bootlegger100.com domain.

source_review.facts_scope: The organizer confirms the April 17, 2027 timed cycling race, open registration, 85-mile / approximately 7,250-foot long course, 58-mile / approximately 4,500-foot short course, Lenoir venue, schedule, support rules, and Maple Sally Road identity. The organizer-linked GPX downloads remain labeled 2026, so final 2027 rider communications override route-file or schedule changes. Facts from the unrelated Georgia trail-running event must not be used.

logistics.explanation: Jason Lopez notes "the course was clearly marked with orange course making tape and big orange signs with arrows" and praises well-stocked aid stations plus post-race burritos. Lenoir offers municipal parking lots where "Car/Van/RV camping" is allowed, with packet pickup Friday evening and Saturday morning. RFID timing and police-escorted neutral rollout show solid operational foundation.

length.explanation: The official 2027 long course is 85 miles, with a 58-mile alternative. That is a substantial endurance day without the ultra-distance scale of the retired 100-plus-mile alignment. Approximately 7,250 feet of climbing keeps the 85 meaningfully harder than its mileage alone suggests.

technicality.explanation: K-Dogg describes descents with "dump trucks of marbles strewn everywhere" that caused hand cramps from "desperately clutching the brakes." Maple Sally Road delivers "17 miles of fiendish up and down" with gradients reaching 21%, while Jason Lopez notes technical descents made "slick in a lot of places" after overnight rain create serious bike handling demands. More technical than most — comparable to Belgian Waffle Ride San Diego.

elevation.explanation: The organizer publishes approximately 7,250 feet of climbing for the 85-mile course and 4,500 feet for the 58. The long route reaches the Grandfather Ranger District and Maple Sally Road, making sustained climbing and repeatable low-cadence power central rather than incidental.

climate.explanation: A 2023 cycling race report describes a rainy, chilly start followed by warmer conditions, and notes that overnight rain made descents slick. Mid-April weather in the North Carolina foothills can materially change traction and clothing needs without creating a dependable extreme-heat or cold protocol.

altitude.explanation: North Carolina elevations stay well below levels that affect oxygen availability or performance. The course travels through Pisgah National Forest foothills and includes sections on the Blue Ridge Parkway, but maximum elevations remain under 5,000 feet where sea-level lungs function normally. Lower altitude than Gravel Worlds — no thin-air concerns.

adventure.explanation: Wilson Creek Gorge, the Grandfather Ranger District, and Maple Sally Road take the race well beyond a generic downtown fondo. The no-outside-support rule makes riders carry their own contingencies through long mountain sectors, while stocked organizer rest areas keep it short of expedition racing.

prestige.explanation: Pisgah Productions has built regional credibility through the King of Pisgah Series, with riders like Nina Laughlin (elite-level racer) taking overall wins. The race attracts competitors from "many scattered states" according to K-Dogg, though it lacks the national profile or prize purse that draws top-tier professional fields to marquee events.

race_quality.explanation: The official 2027 page publishes a full schedule, separate sign-in/start/finish locations, marked turns, police and sheriff traffic control, stocked rest areas, RFID timing, live results, awards, route links, and a post-race meal. That is a stronger operational record than the event's modest profile suggests.

experience.explanation: Downtown Lenoir gives way to Wilson Creek Gorge, Grandfather Ranger District gravel, and Maple Sally Road before a downhill finish back in town. The landscape, difficult descending, and mountain accumulation give the event a coherent identity instead of a collection of anonymous gravel miles.

community.explanation: K-Dogg describes "a huge crowd of cheerful and polite adventurers" with opportunities for "toccata conversations with riders from many scattered states." The shared suffering of North Carolina mountains creates authentic connections, evidenced by the detailed race reports and ongoing community discussions about tire selection and gearing choices for the demanding course.

field_depth.explanation: The organizer publishes extensive age, open, junior, singlespeed, and tandem categories with timed results, but does not publish a 2027 field cap or current entrant count. Historical results show a serious regional racing field; there is not enough current evidence to claim national-level depth.

value.explanation: BikeReg lists $105 for either the 85- or 58-mile race. That buys timing, stocked rest areas, course marking, traffic control, awards, and post-race food. The value is strongest on the 85; charging the same fee for the 58 is the obvious counterpoint.

expenses.explanation: The $105 entry is moderate, and designated downtown lots permit self-contained vehicle camping at no added lodging cost. Most riders will still need a car, and the course rewards suitable tires, brakes, and low gearing, but Lenoir avoids destination-resort pricing.

final_verdict.one_liner: Wilson Creek Gorge will eat your lunch and serve it back with a side of North Carolina suffering.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Bring climbing durability, disciplined fueling, dependable brakes, and real gravel-descending confidence. The official long course is now 85 miles rather than 100-plus, but 7,250 feet and Maple Sally Road still expose anyone who treats the first half like a short race.
final_verdict.alternatives: Dirty Kanza offers similar distance with less technical punishment if you prefer power over bike handling. For the full Appalachian experience without quite this level of commitment, try Trans-Sylvania Epic's individual stages.
